notes: The corpus contains no Egypt-specific PAPSS participant list and no outbound IPN corridor, so no fact asserts an Egypt-to-Nigeria or Egypt-to-Kenya route beyond PAPSS being the appropriate local-currency rail. Exchange rates are deliberately absent (live facts are out of scope).

entries.subject: ipn_currency_restriction
entries.display: IPN cannot send or receive foreign currency
entries.quote: Transactions are restricted to the Egyptian Pound, with no support for foreign currencies.
entries.notes: Closed set: EGP only / EGP and USD / any currency. Answer: EGP only. Transactions are restricted to the Egyptian Pound, with no support for foreign currencies.

entries.subject: inbound_remittance_launch
entries.quote: The inbound cross‑border use case, launched in December 2024, enables recipients in Egypt to receive funds directly into their accounts or wallets.
entries.notes: Recipients are credited in Egyptian pounds into a bank account or wallet.

entries.subject: ipn_international_remittance_model
entries.value_text: local banks, money transfer operators and exchange houses
entries.display: Inbound remittances run through banks, MTOs and exchange houses
entries.quote: A service that utilizes the Instant Payment Network (IPN) to provide Egyptian expatriates with a fast, secure, and efficient way to send money home. By partnering with local banks, money transfer operators, and exchange houses, it ensures recipients can instantly access funds through bank accounts, mobile wallets and cards.
entries.notes: CBE's IPN page describes an inbound service for Egyptian expatriates only.

entries.subject: papss_purpose
entries.value_text: cross-border payments in local African currencies
entries.display: PAPSS moves money between African countries in local currencies
entries.quote: PAPSS – the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System – is a cross-border, financial market infrastructure enabling payment transactions across Africa.
entries.notes: PAPSS is the rail an Egypt-to-Nigeria or Egypt-to-Kenya payment would use; IPN cannot carry it. The corpus does not state which Egyptian banks are live on PAPSS.

entries.subject: papss_flow_currency
entries.value_text: the originator pays in their own local currency
entries.display: Payer sends in their own currency; beneficiary receives in theirs
entries.quote: An originator issues a payment instruction in their local currency to their bank or payment service provider. 2 The payment instruction is sent to PAPSS. 3 PAPSS carries out all necessary validation checks on the payment instruction. 4 The payment instruction is forwarded to the beneficiary’s bank or payment service provider. 5 The beneficiary’s bank clears the funds to the beneficiary in their local currency.
entries.notes: Five-step flow: originator to bank/PSP, instruction to PAPSS, validation, forwarding, local-currency clearing.

entries.subject: papss_headquarters
entries.quote: 72B El-Maahad El-Eshteraky Street, Roxy, Heliopolis, Cairo 11341, Egypt
entries.notes: Closed set: Cairo / Abu Dhabi / Lagos / Nairobi / Port Louis. Answer: Cairo. PAPSS sits in the same jurisdiction as the CBE.

entries.subject: domestic_currency_rule
entries.display: Domestic transactions must be denominated in EGP
entries.quote: As a general rule, the CBE Law requires transactions conducted in Egypt to be denominated in EGP, subject to certain exceptions.
entries.notes: Closed set: EGP only / USD only / any currency. Under the Central Bank and Banking System Law 194/2020.

entries.subject: fx_account_and_transfer_rights
entries.value_text: yes, through licensed banks or exchange bureaux
entries.display: Residents may hold and transfer foreign currency via licensed institutions
entries.quote: According to Law No 88/2003, individuals and businesses can hold foreign currency in Egypt, have local bank accounts denominated in foreign currency, buy foreign currency, and transfer it abroad. This law allows an individual or business to engage in foreign currency transactions, but it requires the use of banks or foreign exchange bureaus that are licensed to trade in foreign currencies.
entries.notes: The guide cites Law 88/2003, which has since been replaced by Law 194/2020; the substance is repeated in ADSERO's reading of the 2020 law.

entries.subject: commercial_fx_documentation
entries.value_text: supporting documents must justify the transfer
entries.display: Commercial outbound FX transfers need supporting documents
entries.quote: Commercial transactions must be supported with specific documents to justify the transfer.
entries.notes: Banks have also been instructed to prioritise essential imports (food, medical).

entries.subject: physical_fx_movement_approval
entries.display: Importing or exporting foreign currency needs prior CBE approval
entries.quote: while the import and export of foreign currencies require prior CBE approval
entries.notes: Transfers through registered banks do not need individual approval; physical movement does.
